mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, which in turn depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and lower corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.5pp, or if the correlation between UNRATE changes and 5-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a weakening consumer demand, which leads to lower corporate revenues and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS drops > 2% MoM, or if the correlation between RSAFS changes and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side, which leads to increased economic activity and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO rises > 1% MoM, or if the correlation between INDPRO changes and 60-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure combined with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% MoM, or if the joint effect of these conditions on 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs in a month signals a strong labor market, which leads to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000, or if the correlation between PAYEMS changes and 5-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decrease by more than 10% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases by more than 0.3 percentage points, it signals a weakening demand and labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST drops > 10% MoM and UNRATE rises > 0.3pp
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where HOUST drops > 10% MoM and UNRATE rises > 0.3pp, or if the joint effect of these conditions on 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a strong economic growth, which leads to increased corporate earnings and investor confidence, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where GDPC1 rises > 1% QoQ, or if the correlation between GDPC1 changes and 60-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
